name: DEWF Saturday Night Extreme, 23 August 1997 (season return)

date.source: The card's own subject line, "DEWF - Saturday Night Extreme for 08/23/1997!", msg_id UeaU3te3YxgJ, posted 28 Aug 1997.

appearances.note: DEWF World Heavyweight Title match; loses the title to Kevin Nash (unminted).

notes: The fed's own first posted show since a 14-month newsgroup silence caused by a posting-gateway failure (explained in a third party's own framing post served elsewhere in this wing). Three of the fed's titles change hands on this single card: Kevin Nash over Shane Douglas for the World Heavyweight Championship, Scott Hall over The Giant for the Intercontinental Championship, and The Razor Boys over Blondes 3:16 for the World Tag Team Championship. Also name-checks a fourth, already-standing DEWF Trios Championship (held by The Razor Boys and Diamond Dallas Page) with no dated change recorded anywhere this project holds.

name: DEWF Saturday Night Extreme, 11 October 1997 (new Commissioner installed)

date.source: The card's own subject line, "DEWF Saturday Night Extreme for 10/11/97!!!", msg_id d7WtgGDC-tkJ, posted 15 Oct 1997; a companion advance-card post (msg_id nMTh0bWpV9YJ) confirms the same date.

notes: Opens on a real-world dedication to "Flyin'" Brian Pillman, the real professional wrestler who had died the week before -- the fed dedicates the rest of the month's shows to his memory. Scott Hall wins a three-way dance (aided by Kevin Nash's interference) against The Giant and Masahiro Chono for the vacant Intercontinental Championship; "Nature Boy" Ric Flair is then introduced on-air as the new DEWF Commissioner, replacing Gary Hart, who cannot return to the role after being attacked by Hall weeks earlier. The Road Warriors retain the World Tag Team Championship against a team billed as "The 2Wo" (Hulk Johnson & Diesel). Kevin Nash retains the World Heavyweight Championship in a rematch against Phil La Fon, then is given a surprise Rumble In The Jungle II opponent, Shawn Michaels -- both events outside this project's own 1997 read window.

name: DEWF Saturday Night Extreme, 30 August 1997

date.source: The card's own subject line, "DEWF Saturday Night Extreme for 08/30/1997!", msg_id C87zSF4ikcUJ.

notes: Not served as a page. Scott Hall retains the Intercontinental Championship against Raven; "The Shadow" Michael Monroe retains the World Light Heavyweight Championship against touring Michinoku Pro rookie Masato Yakashiji (this wing's own first evidence of that title); a DEWF World Heavyweight Title defense by Kevin Nash is also billed on this card.

name: DEWF Saturday Night Extreme, 6 September 1997 (two parts)

date.source: Posted in two parts, both dated in their own subject lines "for 09/06/1997": Part One (msg_id OVOBtb-l9lUJ, posted 12 Sep 1997) and Part Two (msg_id FR33alCNG3IJ, posted 15 Sep 1997).

notes: Not served as a page. Two title changes: Scott Hall retains the Intercontinental Championship against The Giant, then attacks Commissioner Gary Hart to avoid being stripped of it over the tainted win; The Road Warriors win a three-way dance (over The Razor Boys and Blondes 3:16) for the World Tag Team Championship; Phil La Fon, a mystery challenger, upsets Kevin Nash for the World Heavyweight Championship in Part Two.
